requirements.evidence: Contract matched exactly: CreateQueue.php:15, UpdateQueue.php:14, SetQueueAccess.php:16, QueuePermission Call='call', QueueAccess model (table/fillable/cast/relations), migration with cascading FKs + unique pair, QueuePolicy create/update/manageAccess/call, and authorization added in CallNextTicket.php:32 and Ticket.php:99-105 in the required order. Edge handling present: trim/1-255 (CreateQueue.php:20-26), slug default/explicit slugify, per-entity uniqueness with race catch, own-slug allowed (UpdateQueue.php:42), empty list revokes with no log when no row (SetQueueAccess.php:36-55), corrupted non-array permissions denied (QueuePolicy.php:66-69). Flaw: unique-violation detection is over-broad and non-portable (CreateQueue.php:59-68, UpdateQueue.php:79-83); factory entity alignment mutates a caller-supplied queue.

conventions.evidence: Follows most conventions: domain writes in one action per use case, authorization inside each action via Gate/policy, deliberate $fillable on QueueAccess, reversible generated-style migration, docs and CHANGELOG kept in sync. Clear deviations: no Pest/PHPUnit tests at all though conventions require test-first for every feature; QueueAccessFactory hand-rolls entity reconciliation in afterMaking/afterCreating (database/factories/QueueAccessFactory.php:32-72) instead of the simple factory composition the project uses.

security.evidence: Every write authorizes server-side: CreateQueue.php:17, UpdateQueue.php:16, SetQueueAccess.php:18, CallNextTicket.php:32, Ticket.php:103. QueuePolicy is the single source of truth and denies non-members, crosses entities and corrupted non-array permissions (QueuePolicy.php:45-69). All input is validated (name/slug length and emptiness, permission strings whitelisted via QueuePermission::cases(), cross-entity pair check); mass assignment limited by $fillable; no user output/escaping surface, no secrets. No weakness found.

tests.evidence: change.diff touches 13 files and contains no tests/ files; a search of change.diff for 'test', 'pest' or 'phpunit' yields no matches. None of the new actions, policy, model, factory, migration or the two changed call paths has a test, and the unauthorized/inactive/race paths are unverified.

simplicity.evidence: Reasonable reuse of Gate/policy and the enum, but isUniqueViolation is copy-pasted verbatim in CreateQueue.php:59-68 and UpdateQueue.php:79-83, and QueueAccessFactory.php:32-72 adds an afterMaking branch that cannot run for normal factory usage plus an afterCreating force-update hack to align entities.

readability.evidence: Actions are short and clearly named; policy methods are focused with useful docblocks. Deductions: QueueAccessFactory's nested alignEntities/afterCreating logic is hard to follow, and CHANGELOG.md:12 is a single ~900-character bullet that is difficult to review.

scope.evidence: All 13 changed files serve the task: four actions, enum, model, factory, migration, policy, the two call paths that must enforce 'call', plus the three required doc/CHANGELOG updates. No delete action, no UI, no unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests at all, violating the project's test-first rule and leaving the grant/revoke, cross-entity, race, inactive-queue and unauthorized-call paths unverified.

isUniqueViolation treats every SQLSTATE 23000 as a slug duplicate (masking foreign-key violations) and matches 'UNIQUE'/'Duplicate' case-sensitively, so a PostgreSQL 23505/'duplicate key' race would still leak a raw QueryException instead of a ValidationException.

The factory guarantees a same-entity pair by force-updating the entity of whichever queue was supplied, so an explicitly mismatched queue passed by a caller is silently re-pointed to the membership's entity instead of being left/validated; afterMaking's relationLoaded branch is effectively dead code.
The identical unique-violation helper is duplicated in both actions instead of being shared or expressed once.
The single Added bullet is an enormous run-on line; Keep a Changelog entries should be short, scannable bullets.
The casts() docblock says array<string, string>, but a Laravel casts array maps attribute names to cast type strings, so the annotation is misleading.

review.summary: The change implements the queue lifecycle actions, the queue_access table/model/factory, the SetQueueAccess grant/revoke flow with audit logging, the QueuePolicy and enforcement in both ticket call paths, plus the required docs and CHANGELOG updates, and it is well scoped. It ships no tests, which violates the project's test-first convention and leaves the authorization and race paths unverified, and the unique-violation helper is both duplicated and over-broad/non-portable; therefore it needs changes before merging.
